title: Gastrointestinal involvement and diet in cystinosis
summary: Cystinosis is a rare disease with an impact on all organs in the body. In most patients, the kidneys are primarily affected. Due to medications and cystinosis itself, patients report symptoms in the stomach and the intestines, e.g., nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain. We want to assess in detail which of these symptoms occur in patients with cystinosis, and we want to find out whether there is a correlation with diet and body composition. This is why we gather data via questionnaires, interviews, and additional measurements. With these new insights, we hope to improve medical care for patients with cystinosis.

interventions.name:
Cross-sectional study of people with cystinosis visiting the cystinosis outpatient clinic at the RoMed hospital in Rosenheim, Germany.
The following tools will be used:
* the Gastrointestinal Symptoms Rating Scale - Irritable Bowel Syndrome (GSRS-IBS) and the Bristol Stool Form Scale (BSFS) includ

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Appointment at the multiprofessional cystinosis outpatient clinic at the RoMed hospital Rosenheim, Germany, within the duration of the study
Consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
No consent to participate in the study
Unavailability
BIA:
* Patients <10 years of age due to limited reference values
* Patients >10 years of age: Implanted automatic devices, e.g., pacemaker, defibrillator, pregnancy
